decisions.reason: Still being marketed into 2025, this booster system sits squarely in the firm's core coolant-management business, so sunk development effort and visible strategic commitment make withdrawal unlikely.

The centrifuge remains closely aligned with the firm's established filtering and sustainability-focused offering, which encourages management to continue supporting it rather than admit an early reversal.
As a multi-model nozzle line embedded in the existing coolant portfolio, it likely benefits from broad system-selling logic and is especially likely to be retained.
Although somewhat more adjacent than core, the scraper belt chip conveyor still fits the firm's automation and material-flow direction, so management would usually give it further time on the market.
This magnetic belt chip conveyor reinforces the firm's established chip-handling systems portfolio, making continued market presence more likely than a near-term exit.
The hinged belt chip conveyor is close enough to the firm's existing conveying activities that accumulated investment and portfolio breadth argue for keeping it rather than dropping it now.
